The basics

What is DIR Floortime?

DIR stands for Developmental, Individual differences, and Relationship-based. It's a framework for understanding how each child develops. Floortime is the playful, hands-on way of putting it into practice: joining your child where they are, following their lead, and building connection and new abilities through the things they already love.

Rather than drilling isolated skills, Floortime supports the foundations underneath them: regulation, engagement, two-way communication, problem solving, and emotional thinking.

D

Developmental

We meet your child at their current developmental stage and build up from there, one meaningful step at a time.

I

Individual differences

We honor the unique way your child takes in, processes, and responds to the world around them.

R

Relationships

Real growth happens through warm, trusting relationships, so connection always comes first.

In practice

What a Floortime session looks like

To your child, it looks like play. Underneath, every moment is intentional.

Following your child's lead

We start with what your child is drawn to, whether that's trains, water play, or a favorite show, and join them there.

Regulation comes first

We pay close attention to your child's sensory profile and help them feel calm, safe, and ready to connect.

Building back-and-forth

We gently stretch play into longer back-and-forth exchanges, using gestures, sounds, words, or ideas.

Just-right challenge

Once your child is engaged, we add playful problems to solve so they can grow at their own pace.

Who Floortime can help

Floortime can be used with children of every developmental profile. Families often come to us for support with:

AutismADHDPDA (Persistent Drive for Autonomy)Developmental delaysDown syndromeSensory processing differencesSocial and emotional developmentCommunication and connection

Social-emotional learning

Social and emotional growth, through play

Social-emotional skills grow out of relationships. In Floortime, we support the building blocks that make things like friendships, sharing feelings, and working through frustration possible, in ways that feel natural to your child and never ask them to mask who they are.

Solving problems together

Children learn to stay in long back-and-forth exchanges with a trusted adult to figure something out, like getting the lid off a container, finding a hidden toy, or building something together. Along the way, they practice reading facial expressions and gestures, showing what they want, and noticing how others respond. This shared problem solving builds flexibility, cooperation, and a growing sense of self.

Using ideas to share feelings

Through pretend play and conversation, children begin to use ideas to show what they want, think, and feel. A stuffed animal might be scared of the dark, or a toy car might be upset it lost the race. Playing out feelings like these with a partner who joins in helps children understand emotions, put them into words or play, and imagine what someone else might be feeling.

Parent coaching

Floortime doesn't stop when the session ends

You are the most important person in your child's world, so you're at the center of Floortime. We coach you during sessions and help you find simple, realistic ways to use Floortime in everyday moments like bath time, meals, car rides, and play.

Coaching in the moment

We model, then hand the play back to you, with gentle feedback as you go.

Ideas that fit your life

No extra hour of homework. Floortime fits into routines you already have.

Understanding your child

Learn to read your child's cues, sensory needs, and ways of connecting.

Support for the whole family

Siblings and caregivers can join in, so connection grows at home.

Good to know

DIR Floortime questions, answered

Do you offer DIR Floortime in Murfreesboro?
Yes. Cultivate Play provides DIR Floortime in Murfreesboro and across Rutherford County, including Smyrna and La Vergne. Sessions happen in your home or community, at our Murfreesboro office at 1810 Ward Drive, or by telehealth anywhere in Tennessee.
Is DIR Floortime covered by insurance?
We weave Floortime into our occupational therapy sessions, which are billed as occupational therapy. We're in-network with Blue Cross Blue Shield, TennCare Select, and BlueCare. For other plans, we offer private pay (card, cash, or HSA) and can provide a superbill to submit for reimbursement. Katie Beckett Waiver and IEA funding may also apply. We're also a TEIS (Tennessee Early Intervention System) provider for children from birth to age 3.
Are you a TEIS provider?
Yes. Cultivate Play is a provider with TEIS (Tennessee Early Intervention System), which serves children from birth to age 3 with developmental delays or disabilities. If your child is enrolled in TEIS, ask your service coordinator about receiving services with us.
How is DIR Floortime different from ABA?
Both are used with autistic children, but they start from different places. ABA (applied behavior analysis) generally uses structured teaching and reinforcement to build specific behaviors and skills. DIR Floortime is developmental and relationship-based. It follows your child's lead and interests and focuses on regulation, connection, communication, and emotional development, with new skills growing out of that foundation.
Can DIR Floortime help with social skills?
Yes. Rather than teaching scripted social skills, Floortime builds the foundations underneath them: staying connected in back-and-forth play, solving problems together with another person, and using ideas and pretend play to express feelings. That way, social growth comes from genuine connection.
What ages do you work with?
Children and teens, ages 0 to 18. Floortime looks different at every age, from floor play with toddlers to shared interests and problem solving with older kids and teens.
Do parents take part in sessions?
Yes, and we encourage it. Parent coaching is a core part of how we use Floortime, so you'll leave sessions with ideas you can use during everyday routines at home.
How do we get started?
The easiest first step is a free phone consultation. We'll talk about your child and family and whether we're the right fit. Prefer to skip the call? Have your pediatrician fax a referral to (615) 617-5873 and we'll take it from there.
